cues: Statement announces a rate cut 'in light of the implications of global developments' and 'muted inflation pressures', the language of the 2019 mid-cycle adjustment.
Three dissents: James Bullard wanted a larger cut, while two others wanted no change. That matches the September 2019 meeting.
The no-change dissenters preferred to keep the range at '2 percent to [RANGE]', which fits 2 to 2-1/4 percent. That was the range in place before the September 2019 cut.
The text says household spending was rising at a strong pace while business fixed investment and exports had weakened, consistent with Q3 2019 data.
Lael Brainard is listed as a voter, consistent with the 2019 Board.
